result.description:
Arais Care Pty Ltd is a dedicated NDIS service provider committed to delivering high-quality, person-centred support to people living with disability. We empower participants to achieve independence, dignity, social inclusion, and an improved quality of life through compassionate and professional care.
We are currently seeking a dedicated and compassionate Residential Care Officer to join our team in Dirranbandi, Queensland, a remote community. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced care professional looking to build a rewarding career while making a meaningful difference in the lives of people living with disability.
Key Responsibilities
•	Ensure the safety, well-being, and dignity of residents with disability in a residential care setting.
•	Assess individual needs of NDIS participants to develop and implement personalised support, training, and life skills programs.
•	Support and empower residents to build independence, enhance daily living skills, and improve overall quality of life.
•	Facilitate and encourage resident participation in community activities to promote inclusion and social engagement.
•	Conduct client interviews to identify personal, emotional, and social challenges impacting their wellbeing.
•	Monitor and record resident progress, updating support plans as needed and maintaining accurate documentation.
•	Identify local resources and services related to health, housing, employment, and other areas relevant to NDIS participants.
•	Deliver structured skill-building and activity programs with limited supervision, both individually and as part of a team.
•	Liaise with families, support coordinators, community groups, service providers, and government agencies to ensure coordinated care.
•	Provide care and support in group homes and other supported accommodation settings, assisting with daily routines and personal tasks.
•	Assist with meal planning, preparation, and cooking according to resident needs and dietary requirements.
•	Help residents manage behavioural challenges by implementing Behaviour Support and Management Plans.
•	Refer participants to relevant allied health professionals, services, or community supports as appropriate.
•	Advocate for residents' rights and preferences in all aspects of care and community engagement.
•	Prepare reports, care documentation, and funding submissions in line with NDIS compliance and service requirements.
•	Respond to general enquiries, assist with special projects, and contribute to a safe, supportive, and person-centred environment.
•	Participate in team meetings, training, supervision, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
•	Work effectively and independently in a remote community environment.
Essential Requirements
•	Completed at least a Diploma OR an overseas bachelor degree, preferably in Nursing or a related field; alternatively, at least three years of relevant experience may substitute for formal qualifications.
•	Minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience in disability support, residential care, aged care, or community services.
•	Willingness to work and live in Dirranbandi, Queensland (Remote).
•	Strong interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•	Ability to work rotating shifts, including weekends, sleepovers, public holidays, and overnight shifts.
•	Current First Aid and CPR Certificate.
•	Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance, or ability to obtain.
•	Police Clearance Certificate and ability to meet relevant character requirements.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
•	Understanding of person-centred practice and the rights, dignity, and choices of people with disability.
Desirable
•	Experience supporting participants with complex behaviours, psychosocial disability, or high-intensity support needs.
•	Knowledge and understanding of NDIS Practice Standards.
•	Experience with Positive Behaviour Support.
•	Medication competency.
•	Manual handling training.
•	Previous experience working in a rural or remote community.
•	Strong ability to adapt to the unique needs and challenges of remote service delivery.
What We Offer
•	Full-time permanent employment – minimum 38 hours per week.
•	Potential visa sponsorship for suitably qualified and eligible international candidates.
•	Supportive and inclusive workplace culture.
•	Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
•	Career progression within a growing organisation.
•	Opportunity to work in a unique remote Queensland community.
•	Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people living with disability.
How to Apply
To apply, please submit:
•	Your current resume (CV).
•	A cover letter outlining your suitability for the role.
•	Copies of relevant qualifications and licences/certificates.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.
Arais Care Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and non-discriminatory recruitment practices. We encourage applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, disability, cultural background, or ethnicity.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen.

We're a well-respected not-for-profit that's been serving society's most vulnerable for over 170 years. Each year, we achieve life-changing outcomes for more than 40,000 people who rely on our person-centred support. And now, we're extending our reach and impact even further.

As a Senior Case Manager - Supporting Recovery, you'll be key to our mission to enrich lives and strengthen communities. Working within our Community & Mission team, you'll provide trauma-informed, recovery-oriented case management to victim-survivors of family, domestic and sexual violence (FDSV), supporting people to move beyond crisis and achieve their recovery goals.

Be welcomed into a compassionate, respectful and purpose-driven community where we don't just talk about values-we live them.

Your opportunity

As our Senior Case Manager - Supporting Recovery, you will provide specialist case management to victim-survivors of family, domestic and sexual violence who are in the recovery phase following crisis. Through comprehensive assessment, collaborative recovery planning, advocacy and service coordination, you'll empower clients to achieve meaningful recovery outcomes while ensuring services are delivered safely, ethically and in line with best practice.

You'll also provide leadership across the Supporting Recovery Program by mentoring case managers, contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and supporting complex decision-making that strengthens outcomes for both clients and the broader service.

With integrity and resilience, you will:

Deliver trauma-informed, recovery-oriented case management to clients with complex needs.

Lead the management of high-risk and complex cases while mentoring fellow practitioners.

Develop collaborative recovery plans through assessment, advocacy and coordinated service delivery.

Build strong partnerships with clients, CatholicCare, NSW Health and specialist agencies.

Contribute to continuous improvement and best-practice service delivery.

What you'll bring

You are an experienced, compassionate and resilient case management professional who thrives in complex environments and shares our values of Integrity, Justice, Compassion and Excellence.

You will also need:

University qualification in Social Work, Psychology, Welfare or Community Services.

Minimum three years' experience in family and domestic violence recovery case management.

Experience managing complex cases involving trauma, mental health and intersecting vulnerabilities.

Current NSW Driver Licence.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Ideally, you will also have:

AASW social work accreditation

Leadership and mentoring experience.

Knowledge of OOHC legislation and child protection practices.

Experience in trauma-informed and recovery-oriented practice.

Strong stakeholder engagement skills.

Confidence managing high-risk situations.

Why Anglicare?

We provide meaningful opportunities and choice, both for the individuals and communities we support and the dedicated people here who make it happen.

At Anglicare, you'll get the security, stability and opportunities that come with a strong, well-established organisation that's ready for the future. You'll belong to a community of kind, humble and respectful people of all faiths and backgrounds. You will also be supported to gain new knowledge, deepen your experience and expertise, and shape a rewarding career.

Pay less tax with salary packaging.

Up to $2,650 tax free for meals and entertainment.

Ongoing professional development and leadership training.

Exclusive discounts with over 400 retailers.

Employee Assistance Program and Fitness Passport.

We're many services, with one purpose, to meet people where they are and walk with them. At Anglicare, we believe everyone is Made for Connection, with God, with each other, and with the places we call home. But sometimes, life unravels. That's where we step in, in Community and Mission, offering hope, support, and presence. From food relief to chaplaincy, crisis care to caring for the wellbeing of the elderly, every moment of connection matters. And it's not just what we do. It's how we do it: side-by-side, with compassion and care.

Are you ready for a career that means more?

To apply for this role, please click the Apply button and submit your r sum and cover letter. All applicants will receive a response.

Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the customers and communities we support. While we are guided by our Christian-based values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds who share our commitment to serving others. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all ages, genders, abilities and cultural backgrounds.

Position: Pastrycook
Type: Full-time
Employer: San Antonio Group Pty Ltd
Location: Kirribilli NSW 2061
Salary: $79,423 - $89,423 p/a
About the Business
San Antonio Group Pty Ltd is a well-established bakery specialising in the production of traditional baked goods and confectionery products. The company prepares a wide range of fresh breads, pastries, cakes, desserts, and specialty items daily using both traditional and modern techniques. Products are supplied directly to customers through its retail outlet in Kirribilli, with a strong emphasis on ingredient sourcing, quality control, food safety compliance, and customer satisfaction. Renowned for its commitment to consistency, innovation in recipes, and high presentation standards, the business values integrity, teamwork, and excellence in every batch. The workplace culture fosters a supportive, hygienic, and collaborative environment where staff take pride in delivering exceptional baked goods to the local community.
About the Position
The Pastrycook plays a vital role in San Antonio Group Pty Ltd’s daily operations, responsible for preparing and producing a diverse range of high-quality pastries, cakes, and baked goods according to established recipes and standards. This position involves hands-on production from ingredient preparation through to finishing and packaging, ensuring all items meet the bakery’s strict quality, freshness, and presentation requirements. The role is essential to maintaining the business’s reputation for excellence and supporting timely supply to retail customers in a fast-paced bakery environment.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare and produce a wide range of pastries, cakes and other baked goods in accordance with San Antonio Group's established recipes, production methods and quality standards.
Measure, weigh and prepare ingredients, ensuring all raw materials meet required quality and freshness standards.
Mix, laminate, shape and proof doughs and pastry products using both manual techniques and commercial bakery equipment.
Prepare a variety of pastry fillings, creams, icings and decorative finishes for baked products.
Monitor proofing, baking processes and oven temperatures to ensure products are baked consistently and meet quality and presentation standards.
Coordinate the production process, including preparing, baking, cooling, finishing and packaging bakery products to meet daily production schedules.
Decorate cakes, pastries and desserts using glazes, creams, icings and other finishing techniques to achieve high presentation standards.
Operate and maintain commercial bakery equipment, including mixers, dough sheeters, moulders and ovens, ensuring safe and efficient operation.
Maintain a clean, hygienic and organised work area by cleaning equipment, utensils, baking trays and production areas in accordance with food safety and workplace health and safety requirements.
Requirements
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in Baking or a related field.
Minimum 1 year of relevant experience as a Pastrycook or in a similar role.
Strong technical skills in pastry production, dough handling, laminating, baking techniques, and cake decoration.
Sound knowledge of food safety and hygiene regulations, with the ability to maintain a clean and safe working environment.
Excellent attention to detail, time management skills, and the ability to work efficiently under pressure to meet production schedules.
Good interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively as part of a small team.
Physical fitness and stamina to stand for extended periods and handle manual tasks.
How to Apply
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Accord

We are currently seeking enthusiastic and motivated Community Support Workers to provide high-quality support to individuals attending our Day Services and Group Programs across our Community Campuses in Melbourne's north and west, including Greensborough, Glenroy and Sydenham.

As a Community Support Worker, you will work a variety of shifts between 8:30am and 4:30pm, Monday to Friday.

Positions are offered on a casual basis, with the potential for permanent employment for the right candidates.

The Position

Participate in a range of appropriate programs and activities (recreational, pre-vocational, education and social) aimed at increasing the individual's skills and access to and participation in the community

Provide the highest level of support for all individuals supported and ensure each person supported is treated with respect that enhances their personal worth, dignity and rights, at all times

Assist in achieving individual's, team and service goals and objectives.

Seek ways of improving the standards of service by working closely with colleagues, relevant line managers and contributing to meetings

Maintain a high level of service for all individual's and ensure the health, wellbeing and safety of all people supported and staff is maintained at all times

Support the identified needs of individuals in relation to their particular life circumstances

Ensure that where required attendance to personal care needs of clients is undertaken in a professional, empathetic and timely manner

You will have experience liaising with families and circles of support, service providers and community groups, sound written & communication skills, able to multi-task and work under pressure and capable of working independently with an individual or group of people.

Successful applicants must be eligible for a NDIS screening check, hold a valid Australian Drivers Licence, Working with Children check and First Aid Level 2 certificate. 

Experience in the disability sector and-or possession of a relevant qualification will be highly regarded.

Above all, patient care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer:

Hourly rate: $32.87 to $51.81 (inclusive of causal loading) plus 12% Superannuation

Casual positions available

We offer a range of salary packaging options tailored to your employment status such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses - up to $18,550 as a permanent employee and a percentage of your earnings as a casual

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options & well-being programs

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

St John of God Accord (SJGA) complies with the NDIS Commission and all prospective employees are required to apply for your NDIS Check to ensure the safety and wellbeing of people with a disability.

For enquiries contact Steven Williams, Manager Community Campuses and Employment Services on (03) 8468 1156.

Please note: If suitable candidates are identified, shortlisting and interviews may begin before the advertisement closes.
